extracted.intended_audience: ERC peer reviewers (Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators, Remote Referees) for the ERC Advanced Grant (AdG) call
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation rules for reviewers assessing ERC Advanced Grant proposals in the two-step panel-based peer review (Step 1 remote review of Part B1; Step 2 remote review of full proposal and interviews). Covers criteria, scoring, conflicts of interest, roles, and review conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion of evaluation and is at the core of the peer review evaluation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied primarily to the ground‑breaking nature, ambition and feasibility of the Research Project and to the intellectual capacity, creativity and commitment of the Principal Investigator. No other criteria than the evaluation elements applying to the Evaluation Criterion defined in the ERC WP must be considered. Incorrect application of the criterion is a procedural error that may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Ground‑breaking nature and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent does the proposed research address important challenges? To what extent are the objectives ambitious and beyond the state of the art (e.g. novel concepts and approaches or development between or across disciplines)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated under the Research Project element at both steps, with emphasis on ground-breaking nature and ambition. Panel comments should explain how ground‑breaking/ambitious objectives are (or are not) met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Scientific approach (feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent is the outlined scientific approach feasible bearing in mind the ground‑breaking nature and ambition of the proposed research (based on the Extended Synopsis)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility of the scientific approach is assessed at Step 1 based on Part B1 (Extended Synopsis). Detailed methodology is assessed at Step 2 using the full proposal (Part B2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Methodology and working arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent are the proposed research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project (based on the research proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed in detail at Step 2. Reviewers should judge whether methodology and organisation are appropriate given the ground‑breaking ambition; if weaknesses are revealed in panel discussion they must be documented in the panel comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Timescales, resources and PI commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent are the proposed timescales, resources, and PI’s commitment adequate and properly justified (based on the research proposal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of resources and commitment is carried out at Step 2. Reviewers should not recommend resources cuts at Step 1. Any recommended budget reductions at Step 2 must be justified, documented, and explained in the panel comment; cuts across-the-board are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct ground‑breaking research? To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative and original thinking? To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels evaluate the PI's intellectual capacity, creativity and commitment with focus on track record and ability to execute the project. Consideration may be given to preprints (properly referenced/DOI). Reviewers should take into account phase of transition to independence, diverse career paths, noteworthy community contributions, career breaks, and pandemic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step‑specific assessment focus (Step 1 vs Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility of the scientific approach is assessed at Step 1. The detailed scientific approach (methodology, timescales, and resources included) is assessed at Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 1: Panel Members act as generalists and review Part B1 (extended synopsis + PI CV/track record). Step 2: Panel Members and Remote Referees review full proposal (Parts B1 and B2), resources, budget table and time commitment; interviews take place and are taken into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual review deliverables (marks and PI qualitative assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explanatory comments for the Research Project and the Principal Investigator and award an overall mark for the Research Project and an overall qualitative assessment for the PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal marks: integers or halves, range 5 (Outstanding) to 1 (Non-competitive). Use full range recommended. PI qualitative options: Outstanding / Excellent / Very Good / Good / Non-competitive. Remote Referees use a three-option recommendation: highly recommended / recommended / not recommended. Marks and PI assessments must be consistent with comments. Individual reviews must be submitted by ERCEA deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards for individual reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviews should be of good quality, genuine, succinct but substantial, and polite; comments should take the form of a statement and explanation of key strengths and weaknesses of the proposal, in light of the evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantial explanatory comments; avoid mere description or summary. Use dispassionate, analytical, and unambiguous language; grammatically correct, complete, clear sentences with no jargon. Ensure comments align with marks/recommendations. Critical comments must be constructive. Avoid self-declaration of insufficient expertise. Avoid reference to applicant’s age, nationality, gender, religion, personal matters, or Host Institution (Host Institution standing is not an ERC criterion). Be aware of unconscious bias (gender & diversity). Avoid dismissive statements about PI, proposed science, or field. Do not compare directly with other proposals or previous assessments. Avoid copy‑paste from proposal or other experts' reviews. When assessing achievements focus on scientific content; refrain from surrogate measures (e.g. Journal Impact Factors). Avoid comments on ethical and security aspects (these are addressed after scientific evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest rules — explicit list
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of conflicts of interest will be displayed in the online system and experts must confirm absence of conflict when accepting and when submitting reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: I am PI or team member in the proposal; I was involved in the preparation of the proposal; I would benefit should the proposal be accepted or rejected; I am employed/contracted by an entity involved (past 3 years); I am director/trustee/partner or involved in management of an entity involved (past 3 years); I am collaborating scientifically or have done so in past 5 years with the PI; I have/had a mentor/mentee relationship with the PI; family ties/close personal relationship with PI or persons involved; relationship of scientific rivalry/hostility with the PI; I am National Contact Point or working for EEN; I am member of an EU programme committee; any other situation precluding impartial review. It is the expert's responsibility to declare COI. Panel Chair shall avoid assigning proposals to conflicted reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and non‑contact obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing contracts/letters reviewers accept conditions regarding confidentiality and conflict of interest; peer reviewers should not engage in any contact with applicants or beneficiaries about the evaluation, neither during nor after the evaluation is over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During individual remote review there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers. Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts. If a reviewer considers they have insufficient expertise they must inform ERCEA Scientific Officers and the Panel Chair so reassignment can occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of Panel Chairs, Panel Members, PEVs and Remote Referees
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Chairs and Panel Members: familiarisation with proposals, individual remote review of a subset of proposals, participation in panel meetings; Lead Reviewer role for introducing proposals and drafting panel comment. PEVs: help at Step 1 and Step 2 as specialists, do not attend panel meetings. Remote Referees: specialists providing input (usually 2‑5 per proposal), non-paid, deliver individual assessments remotely and do not participate in panel meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Chairs have additional tasks: chair meetings; attend Initial and Final Panel Chairs’ meetings; (re)allocate proposals to panels; assign proposals to Panel Members and Remote Referees; ensure deliverables at required quality; select experts for remote evaluation. Panel Members expected to deliver concise but substantial reviews reflecting both specialist and generalist competence and openness to inter‑/multi-disciplinary perspectives. Panel Evaluators can be used to assist workload and act as specialists when selected. Remote Referees typically assess 1–3 proposals and are approved by Panel Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comment — purpose and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel comment is the key element of information provided to applicants; it should clearly explain the reason(s), respecting the ERC evaluation criterion, which make(s) the proposal succeed or fail in the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead Reviewers draft panel comments reflecting panel discussion; panels must ensure scientific feedback is distinct from budget recommendations (budget recommendations are binding). Panel comments should document weaknesses revealed by panel even if not present in individual reviews. Panel comment must be approved by the Panel Chair and should explain the decision adopted by the panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 scoring categories and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal receives one of the following panel scores at Step 1: A invited; A not invited; B; C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A invited — proposal is excellent and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2 (max 44 per panel). A not invited — proposal is excellent but not ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2. B — high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2. C — not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2. Applicants with B or C may be subject to resubmission restrictions as per ERC WP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 scoring categories and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2 each proposal receives one of the following panel scores: A or B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score A — proposal fully meets ERC's excellence criterion and is recommended for funding, if sufficient funds are available. Score B — proposal meets some but not all elements of the excellence criterion and is not recommended for funding. The assessment takes into account individual reviews, panel discussion, and the applicant interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking methodology and possible voting
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking of proposals is the outcome of a thorough discussion in the panel, excluding Panel Members who have a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consensus decisions are preferred but panels may finalise ranking by voting (e.g., majority vote) or by cumulative ranking systems. A Panel Chair/Member under conflict of interest cannot discuss or vote on the relevant proposal. Final call ranking consolidates results across panels using 'normalised accumulated budget' (NAB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of proposal budget (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2, the panel analyses the budget, its justification and the requested contribution of the proposals being considered for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations for reduction may be made if resources are not justified or costs are excessive; recommendations must be documented and explained in the panel comment for each proposal concerned. Analysis is case-by-case; across-the-board cuts are not allowed. Budget recommendations from the panel are binding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and role of Remote Referees and Panel Evaluators (PEVs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote Referees provide specialist reviews (usually 2–5 per proposal) during Step 2; PEVs are Panel Members from other calls/panels who can assist remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees are selected on the basis of expertise, are non-paid, and typically evaluate 1–3 proposals. Their three-option recommendation (highly recommended / recommended / not recommended) complements Panel Members' generalist reviews. Panel Chairs select and approve remote experts; names published annually after results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multi‑ and inter‑disciplinary proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals of a multi- and interdisciplinary nature are strongly encouraged and are evaluated by the ERC's primary panels, with appropriate external expertise where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can indicate a secondary panel if cross-domain. Panels may flag interdisciplinary proposals and request additional reviews from other panels. Initial allocation is based on applicant preference but may be reallocated by agreement of Panel Chairs to ensure competent and fair evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and eligibility reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment of admissibility and eligibility of submitted proposals is carried out by the ERCEA; however, if an expert considers a proposal to be potentially inadmissible or ineligible during the evaluation process, they should report the case immediately to the ERCEA Scientific Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some proposals may be declared inadmissible or ineligible during or after peer review if non-compliance is confirmed later. Experts must report suspected cases; ERCEA makes final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected reviewers' confidentiality during remote review
rubrics_metrics.description: During the individual remote review process, there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers. Panel Members should not disclose the proposals assigned for their evaluation to other experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality obligations extend to non-discussion before panel meetings and non-disclosure of assigned proposals. If insufficient expertise is felt, inform ERCEA Scientific Officers and Panel Chair for reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and form requirements for review language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use dispassionate, analytical, and unambiguous language. Use grammatically correct, complete, clear sentences with no jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inadmissible content (personal attributes, host institution commentary, societal impact claims). Ensure readability; ERCEA may edit to improve readability or remove clerical errors/inappropriate comments where this does not affect evaluation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain assessment aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use societal impact, Host Institution standing, ethical and security aspects, or Journal Impact Factors as evaluation criteria in the scientific assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Societal impact is explicitly not an ERC evaluation criterion. Ethical and security clearances are performed after scientific evaluation. When assessing applicants' achievements, avoid surrogate measures such as Journal Impact Factors; panels should prioritise qualitative judgement. Funding ID should include only current grants or pending applications to allow overlap checks and is not a complete funding record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliverables of each panel meeting include: ranked list of proposals; panel comments approved by the panel; list of approved Remote Referees (only at Step 1); panel report; panel recommendations (Step 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members/shareholders must ensure deliverables are produced at required quality standards by the end of panel meetings. Panel comments and ranked lists form the basis of feedback to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of independent experts at applicant request
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request that up to three specific persons would not act as peer reviewers in the evaluation of their proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests are confidentially treated by ERCEA; excluded experts may be excluded if evaluation remains possible. If excluded expert is a panel member they will be informed confidentially; in case of Panel Chair exclusion ERCEA may consult Deputy Panel Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission restrictions after Step 1 rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose proposals receive a B or C score in Step 1 may be subject to resubmission restrictions in future calls if specified in the applicable ERC Work Programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check ERC Work Programme for details on restrictions. Panel comments and individual reviews are part of feedback to rejected applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic evaluation tools (SEP) and administrative process
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts work individually using the on-line Commission's Evaluation tool (SEP) for remote evaluation at both Step 1 and Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick Guide and user manuals are provided by the Commission; reviewers must submit reviews via SEP and confirm absence of conflicts in the system. ERCEA sets deadlines for submission via SEP.
